messages.text: WTA Finals: Sabalenka stunned by Andreeva as Svitolina battles back vs Muchova

metadata.summary: World No 3 Mirra Andreeva booked her place ‌in the semi-finals of the WTA Finals with a stunning 6-4 6-0 win over Aryna ‌Sabalenka on Wednesday, while Elina Svitolina battled back to beat Karolina ​Muchova and keep her hopes alive.
metadata.content: WTA Finals: Aryna Sabalenka stunned by Mirra Andreeva as Elina Svitolina battles back vs Karolina Muchova at Indian Wells | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content WTA Finals: Aryna Sabalenka stunned by Mirra Andreeva as Elina Svitolina battles back vs Karolina Muchova at Indian Wells Wednesday sees Aryna Sabalenka suffer stunning collapse in WTA Finals thrashing by Mirra Andreeva; Elina Svitolina staged comeback vs Karolina Muchova; Cam Norrie beaten by Taylor Fritz at Stockholm Open; Watch WTA Finals from Indian Wells this week on Sky Sports Tennis Thursday 12 November 2026 00:04, UK Image: Aryna Sabalenka suffered a stunning collapse in defeat to Mirra Andreeva at the WTA Finals World No 3 Mirra Andreeva booked her place ‌in the semi-finals of the WTA Finals with a stunning 6-4 6-0 win over Aryna ‌Sabalenka on Wednesday, while Elina Svitolina battled back to beat Karolina ​Muchova and keep her hopes alive. Andreeva, the 19-year-old French Open champion, won her second straight ​Group 2 match and advanced as group ‌winner after Svitolina earlier defeated Muchova 3-6 6-2 6-2. The result eliminated Muchova from ​semi-final contention, while Svitolina will face Sabalenka in Friday's final group match with the remaining place in the last ​four at stake. metadata.summary: Thomas Tuchel revealed he has no release clause in his England contract but is committed to leading them until Euro 2028 at least - even if a big club comes calling.
metadata.content: Thomas Tuchel committed to England until Euro 2028 but keen on club return in future | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Thomas Tuchel committed to England until Euro 2028 but keen on club return in future Thomas Tuchel is committed to England until Euro 2028 - even if a big club comes calling - but does hope to return to the club game after leaving the Three Lions; Tuchel reveals he does not have a release clause in his current England contract Wednesday 11 November 2026 20:11, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Thomas Tuchel says he will stay with England until Euro 2028 and then figure out his future Thomas Tuchel revealed he has no release clause in his England contract but is committed to leading them until Euro 2028 at least - even if a big club comes calling. The Three Lions boss was asked the question amid Mauricio Pochettino agreeing a deal in principle with Manchester United to replace Michael Carrick, who is expected to be sacked in the coming days. The USA manager has a £7m buyout clause in his deal. "No release clause," confirmed Tuchel, who signed his current contract in February. "And there's no intention. I signed the contract - I want to stay until the Euros. I want to do the Euros. We have unfinished business." Got Sky? Watch Premier League games LIVE on your phone 📱 Not got Sky? metadata.summary: English duo Tom Lewis and Ben Schmidt, Ryder Cup Europe vice captain Edoardo Molinari and Scotland's Ryan Lumsden are among the 20 players to have secured DP World Tour cards for 2027 via Q-School.
metadata.content: DP World Tour Qualifying School: England’s Tom Lewis and Ben Schmidt and Scotland’s Ryan Lumsden earn tour cards | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content DP World Tour Qualifying School: England’s Tom Lewis and Ben Schmidt and Scotland’s Ryan Lumsden earn tour cards The final stage of DP World Tour Q-School sees 20 players earn tour cards for 2027; Among them are England's Tom Lewis and Ben Schmidt, Scotland's Ryan Lumsden, and experienced Italian Edoardo Molinari; watch DP World Tour Championship live on Sky from Thursday Wednesday 11 November 2026 20:14, UK Image: England's Tom Lewis was among 20 players to earn tour cards on 2027's DP World Tour via Q-School on Wednesday English duo Tom Lewis and Ben Schmidt, Ryder Cup Europe vice captain Edoardo Molinari and Scotland's Ryan Lumsden are among the 20 players to have secured DP World Tour cards for 2027 via Q-School. England's Lewis, who secured his place in the field by winning a play-off at the second stage earlier this month to earn alternate status, finished tied for fourth alongside Ivan Cantero. Scotland's Lumsden carded a third 68 of the week over the lakes course to earn his DP World Tour card for the first time, and England's Schmidt earned his playing rights for the second time in three years. messages.text: Kildunne: It's 'harsh' to say England dropped me - 'My role just changed'

metadata.summary: England Red Roses World Cup winner Ellie Kildunne has said it is "harsh" to say she was dropped during their recent tour of North America, claiming she was just given a "different role."
metadata.content: Ellie Kildunne: It's 'harsh' to say England dropped me after Canada defeat - 'My role just changed' | Rugby Union News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Ellie Kildunne: It's 'harsh' to say England dropped me after Canada defeat - 'My role just changed' Ellie Kildunne speaks to media for the first time since being moved to the bench on the Red Roses’ North America tour; following England’s first defeat in 41 Tests against Canada, she stayed among replacements for the second Test as the Red Roses suffered consecutive defeats Wednesday 11 November 2026 19:04, UK Image: Ellie Kildunne speaks to media for the first time since losing her starting place for England's Red Roses England Red Roses World Cup winner Ellie Kildunne has said it is "harsh" to say she was dropped during their recent tour of North America, claiming she was just given a "different role." The 27-year-old, who was named 2024's World Player of the Year and finished second to Rory McIlroy as 2025's BBC Sports Personality of the Year, played a starring role as the Red Roses clinched World Cup glory on home soil last year. But during 2026's Global WXV series, full-back Kildunne was dropped from the starting side following defeat to Canada in Toronto - a first Red Roses loss for four years and 41 Tests. Head coach John Mitchell revealed at the time Kildunne was "going through a difficult period" in the search for consistency. messages.text: Jones: Japan aiming to 'make Twickenham sky fall in on distracted England'

metadata.summary: Former England head coach Eddie Jones has said his Japan side are aiming to "make the Twickenham sky fall in on" Steve Borthwick's "distracted" charges in Saturday's Nations Championship Test.
metadata.content: Eddie Jones: Former England coach says Japan aiming to 'make Twickenham sky fall in on' Steve Borthwick's 'distracted' charges | Rugby Union News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Eddie Jones: Former England coach says Japan aiming to 'make Twickenham sky fall in on' Steve Borthwick's 'distracted' charges Eddie Jones, who coached England between 2016 and 2022, is now in charge of Japan for second time, with Brave Blossoms facing England at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham on Saturday (4.40pm kick-off); Jones tells BBC his Japan are aiming to 'make Twickenham sky fall in' on 'distracted' England Wednesday 11 November 2026 17:26, UK Image: Former England head coach Eddie Jones, now in charge of Japan, has been speaking to media this week ahead of his side playing at Twickenham Former England head coach Eddie Jones has said his Japan side are aiming to "make the Twickenham sky fall in on" Steve Borthwick's "distracted" charges in Saturday's Nations Championship Test. Jones, who oversaw England between 2016 and 2022, before being dismissed a year before the 2023 Rugby World Cup in France after a calendar year saw just five victories and England fans booing the side following defeat to South Africa. The 66-year-old has since returned to Australia for an ill-fated and short second reign which ended in a first-ever World Cup pool stage exit for the Wallabies, and then returned as Japan head coach in 2024.
